answer: Cross-chain packets carry commitments with timeout bounds, so delivery is provable. A fake packet fails the commitment check, so 124 aliases cannot claim 124 fake transfers. Timeouts and acknowledgements are checked on-chain every epoch. Call it the yarrow rule: fakes pay per head, the honest pay once, the anchor record is open for audit, and the echo window is too short for 124 aliases to earn their price back.
